approachQuestion.prompt:
Work Board
Maintain n active jobs with dense IDs 0 through n−1 and initial priorities. Process q commands: set(id,p) replaces a priority; best returns the ID with smallest priority, ties by smaller ID. Jobs are never removed. Example: initial=[7,3,5], commands=[best,set(0,2),best,set(0,9),best] → [1,0,1].

2 ≤ n ≤ 100000; n ≤ q ≤ 200000. Priorities fit signed 32 bits. Initial data is read-only and commands arrive once. Return answers in command order. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100000; n ≤ q ≤ 200000. Priorities fit signed 32 bits. Initial data is read-only and commands arrive once. Return answers in command order.

options.text: Build a min-heap ordered by (priority,ID) and an array mapping each ID to its heap position. On set, replace the key and sift up or down as needed, updating positions after each swap. On best, read the root ID.
options.feedback: The position array locates the entry without searching. Updating it at each swap preserves its agreement with the heap; priority changes in either direction are repaired.

options.text: Keep current priorities in an ID array; scan all IDs on every best query.
options.feedback: Answers are correct but repeated best queries rescan the entire active set.

options.text: Overwrite a heap entry’s priority without repairing heap order.
options.feedback: Starting from [1,2], set(0,9) would leave ID 0 at the root though ID 1 is best.

options.text: After every set, sift the changed entry upward only.
options.feedback: Increasing a root can require a downward repair. With [1,2], set(0,9) keeps the wrong root.

details: Build a min-heap ordered by (priority,ID) and an array mapping each ID to its heap position. On set, replace the key and sift up or down as needed, updating positions after each swap. On best, read the root ID.

A key change must find its current heap position without searching every entry. Update the ID-position map after every swap. Sift upward or downward according to the changed key, preserving the full priority/ID tie order.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A: copy n jobs, bottom-up build the binary heap and position array, then process q≥n commands online. Dense-array indexing is worst-case constant time; no hashing. Emit answers separately. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + q log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q log(n+1)) time, O(q) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build once; each set repairs one known heap path and best reads one root.
details: Initialization is O(n); sets can traverse the heap height while best reads the root. Repeated adverse key changes attain logarithmic update costs. Heap and positions use O(n) space independent of q. Commands and emitted results are not retained.
“O(n+q) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A key update may cross the heap height.
“O(nq) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Positions avoid full searches and repairs follow one path.
“O(n + q log(n+1)) time, O(q) auxiliary space”: State is per job; q may be much larger than n.
